chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Bakr ibn Abi Bakr, from Zurara ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Glorification of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) is from the Abundant Remembrance of which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spoke: 'Mention Allah with a frequent Mentioning.'

key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ الزَّهْرَاءُ: Fatima al-Zahra, the daughter of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for the Tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi explicitly identifies the Tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra as the specific manifestation of 'Dhikr al-Kathir' (Abundant Remembrance) commanded in the Quran, thereby elevating its status from a recommended practice to one with direct scriptural warrant. By linking this devotional act to the verse in Surah Al-Ahzab, Shia scholarship underscores its role in spiritual purification and its connection to the Ahl al-Bayt's exemplary piety. The chain of narration, featuring key figures like Zurara and Abu Abdullah (Imam al-Sadiq), reinforces its authenticity within the Usuli tradition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Bakr Bin Abu Bakr, from Zurara Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Glorification (Tasbeeh) of Fatima Al-Zahraasws is from the ‘Abundant Zikr’ which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Speaks of [33:41] Mention Allah, with a frequent Mentioning’. From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahaam and Mansour Bin Hazim, and Saeed Al A’raj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Bakr ibn Bukayr from Zurara ibn ‘A’Yun from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra (a.s.) is a form of ‘Often speaking and remembering Allah’ about which Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘Believers, remember Allah very often [33:41] and glorify Him both in the mornings and in the evenings.’” [33:42] It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from abu ‘Usamah Zayd al-Shahham and Mansur ibn Hazim and Sa’id al-‘A’raj from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) a similar Hadith.
